subject: Insurance
title: Insuring Against a Bad Movie
description: A quick, practical guide to Insuring Against a Bad Movie.

hook.text: Film studios insure against actors dying, getting injured, or being arrested mid-production.

buildup.text: Completion bonds guarantee a film gets finished. If the lead actor can't work, the bond company funds the fix.

discovery.text: After Heath Ledger died during filming, insurers paid millions to complete The Imaginarium of Doctor Parnassus.

twist.text: Some actors are considered uninsurable. Studios avoid casting them because no one will cover the production risk.

climax.text: In Hollywood, insurability determines castability. An uninsurable star is an unemployable star.

punchline.text: No insurance, no movie role. Hollywood runs on risk coverage.

quiz.question: What happens when a movie star is deemed uninsurable?
options: Studios avoid casting them because production risk can't be covered
